title: Rabbi Yose ben Nehorai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Avodah Zarah 58a it is related that Rabbi Yohanan ben Arza and Rabbi Yose ben Nehorai were sitting and drinking wine. A certain man came; they said to him, 'Come, serve us a drink.' After he had poured into the cup, it became known that the man was a gentile. One forbade it even for benefit, and one permitted it even for drinking. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: 'The one who forbade forbade rightly,' etc. And in Chullin 56b [supplied locator; matching Davidson passage at 57b] he asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, 'How large a perforation of the windpipe [renders the animal unfit]?' He said to him, 'We learned a complete Mishnah.' He said to him, 'But there was a single ewe — and it lived.' He said to him, 'And on this you rely? But it is a widespread halakhah in Israel,' etc.
And in the Jerusalem Talmud, Moed Katan ch. 1 halakhah 7, he disagrees with Rav Hisda and R"YBL.

Hyman writes that R' Yohanan received from him, as in Bava Metzia 41a, where R' Yohanan says in his name (and Rashi explains that he was R' Yohanan's teacher, while the Tosafot there say he was a Tanna), and R' Yohanan disagrees with him there.
And so we find their disputes in Berakhot ch. 9 halakhah 3.

As for what we find in Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot ch. 8, end of halakhah 1, 'R' Yose ben Nehorai heard what R' Elazar said in the name of R' Hoshaya,' Hyman interprets this to mean that he heard it from R' Hoshaya.
He is also mentioned in Sukkah ch. 3 halakhah 1. Among those who speak in his name we find R' Aha in his name, as in Berakhot ch. 3 halakhah 3 and Sukkah ch. 3 halakhah 9.
R' Berekhia and R' Hiyya his father in his name, as in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana at the beginning of 'Ulekachtem,' and Vayikra Rabbah at the beginning of ch. 30.
R' Yehuda son of R' Simon in his name in Vayikra Rabbah ch. 27 (supplied 'ה', i.e. section 5), Tanhuma 'Emor' (supplied 'אמר־יב').
R' Levi in his name, as in Bereshit Rabbah at the end of ch. 6.
R' Simon in his name, as in Sotah ch. 9 halakhah 5.
R' Shimon bar Ba in his name, as in Niddah at the beginning of ch. 3.

Hyman’s printed notice (II, pp. 733–734) gives Chullin 56b. In Davidson Chullin 57b, R’ Yose ben Nehorai asks about a perforated windpipe and cites the ewe. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi answers him. In Avodah Zarah 58a the two sages ask the man to serve them. Once his identity becomes known, the passage gives both rulings without assigning them individually. For Moed Katan, the print reads chapter 1, halakhah 6, as supported by the passage in the consulted Wikisource text. The supplied transcription and translation give halakhah 7. Bava Metzia 41a ends with R’ Yohanan quoting Nehorai. In the 41b continuation Rashi explicitly calls Nehorai his teacher, and Tosafot describes him as a Tanna. In Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 8:1, R’ Elazar speaks in R’ Hoshaya’s name before R’ Yose hears the teaching and objects. Hyman infers that R’ Yose heard it directly from R’ Hoshaya. The named Vayikra Rabbah 27:5 and Buber Tanchuma Emor 12 separately attest the teaching in Nehorai’s name even though Hyman’s compact printed chapter citation is hard to distinguish.
